title: The "data" URL scheme
summary: Defines the data URL scheme, which lets a small piece of data be placed directly inside a URL instead of being fetched from elsewhere. This is handy for embedding small images or text in a page. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Normally an address tells you where to go to fetch a picture. A data URL is like putting the tiny picture right inside the envelope, so there is nothing to go and get.

questions: how do i embed an image in a url
what is the data uri scheme
subtitle: A URL scheme that puts a small piece of data directly inside the URL itself.

tldr.problem: Some applications that use URLs need to embed small media type data inline instead of pointing at something stored elsewhere.
tldr.mechanism: The data scheme has the form data:[mediatype][;base64],data. The data is either base64 or %xx-escaped, and the media type defaults to text/plain;charset=US-ASCII.
tldr.outcome: It is only useful for short values, since some applications limit URL length, and it makes it hard for firewalls to screen out risky media types.

today: RFC 2397 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Immediate Data in a URL
sections.content:
RFC 2397 defines a new URL scheme, data. It works like 'immediate addressing': a small data item is included in the URL as if it had been included externally.

The scheme is only useful for short values. Some applications limit URL length; for example, URLs inside HTML <A> anchors are limited by the SGML declaration for HTML (RFC 1866), with LITLEN set at 1024. The scheme has no relative URL forms.
sections.eli5: A data URL carries its own small message instead of pointing somewhere else. It only works for small things.

sections.title: Format and Encoding
sections.content:
A data URL looks like data:[<mediatype>][;base64],<data>. The media type is an Internet media type with optional parameters. If it is omitted, it defaults to text/plain;charset=US-ASCII, and text/plain may be left out while a charset parameter is supplied.

If ;base64 appears, the data is base64 encoded. Without it, safe URL characters are written as ASCII and other octets use the standard %xx hex escape. The ;base64 marker is told apart from a parameter because it has no following =. Parameter values should use URL escaping rather than quoted strings if they contain any tspecial, since the quote mark is not a valid URL character.
sections.eli5: After the word data and a colon you say what kind of thing it is, then a comma, then the thing itself.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content:
data:,A%20brief%20note encodes the text/plain string 'A brief note'. A base64 GIF can be placed in an IMG tag's SRC for a small inline image, though the RFC says that image is probably near the limit of utility and larger data is likely unsuitable.

A charset can be given, as in data:text/plain;charset=iso-8859-7,%be%fg%be. The scheme can also pass setup parameters to a helper application for a media type.
sections.eli5: You can hide a short note or a tiny picture right inside the address.

sections.title: Security Notes
sections.content:
Interpreting data in a data URL carries the same security considerations as the given media type. An application should not interpret a data URL marked with a media type its configuration disallows.

Sites using firewall proxies to block certain media types will find it difficult to screen for them when they arrive in data URLs. The RFC also says the effect of long data URLs is unknown, and some software may misbehave when data exceeds its allocated buffer size.
sections.eli5: Because the content is inside the address, guards that check packages by type have a harder time seeing what is inside.
